name: random_split

dataset.curation: chemical component dictionary + curated exclusion lists

filters.sampling: uniform without replacement from the pool

coherence.interpretation: members within a cluster can fall below the identity threshold to each other because centroid linkage compares only to the representative. This over-merges, which is conservative for leakage control but coarsens the split.

split.name: random_protein
split.note: homology is ignored; for comparison only

leakage_verification.note: no homology verification: this split deliberately ignores homology and is reported only as a comparison arm

caveats: AUROC is reported for comparability with the literature, but at a 8.2% positive rate it is not a sufficient summary: the false-positive-rate denominator is the large negative class, so a high AUROC is compatible with low precision. AUPRC (chance = 0.082) and precision in the top L/10 are the metrics that reflect usable output.
random protein split: homologous proteins may appear in both train and test, so these numbers are optimistic and are reported only for comparison against the homology-separated split

comparison.note: ranked by AUPRC: under class imbalance AUROC compresses exactly the differences that matter, and a model must beat the per-residue baselines to have justified its context modelling

warnings: 4 of 62 multi-member clusters contain pairs below the 30% identity threshold (minimum observed 0.071). Centroid linkage compares each sequence only to a cluster representative, so it over-merges. This is conservative for leakage — unrelated proteins sharing a fold never split a homologous pair — but it coarsens the split and reduces the number of independent test families.
